importance_ranking.reason: Extreme visual variation across sub-types — portable cabin, multi-storey labour camp, storage shed, tent structure, container unit. Buyers use the image to identify building type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.
Building type, panel type, and size are primary shortlisting criteria — a buyer needing a labour camp cannot substitute a security cabin. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated or priced.

Indian B2B buyers compare prices aggressively after confirming building type. Price varies substantially across building types and panel specifications, making it a primary decision lever once type and spec are confirmed.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per unit dominates for standard portable cabins and site offices; per sq ft is used for larger labour camps and custom-sized structures. Both units appear in the market — must be shown to prevent price comparison confusion.
importance_ranking.reason: Per unit vs per sq ft creates genuine price comparison confusion for buyers comparing standard cabins against larger custom structures. Unit must be shown alongside price to make comparisons meaningful.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall — market is fragmented across regional fabricators and buyers search by building type and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Installation capability, turnkey supply (design-supply-erect), and project track record are evaluated during vendor selection but only after price and spec shortlisting are complete.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the structure IS — site office, labour camp, storage shed, medical camp are non-interchangeable and carry the largest price delta in the category.
PUF vs GI Sheet vs EPS Panel drives significant price and thermal performance differences — buyers specify panel type based on climate, project duration, and insulation requirement.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers specify required floor area (sq ft) or standard catalogue dimensions (10x10 ft, 10x20 ft) to get accurate quotes — sellers cannot price without knowing the required size.
PUF, EPS, and rock wool cores have distinct thermal performance and price profiles — buyers in hot climates or cold-storage applications specify core type as a primary requirement.

Panel thickness (40mm to 80mm) directly determines thermal insulation rating and structural load capacity — a standard differentiator that affects both price and compliance with project specifications.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to sellers who supply the correct building configuration — a seller specialising in site offices cannot supply event halls or disaster relief shelters.
Defines the structural quality tier and thermal performance — sellers need this to confirm manufacturing capability and to price the structure accurately.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers cannot generate an accurate quote without knowing the required floor area or standard cabin dimensions — this is the primary sizing input for any temporary building.
Single-floor vs G+1 structures require different structural design, foundation approach, and installation complexity — sellers need this to confirm capability and quote accurately.
